paper_title: Entertain, then Cancel: How Thinking Makes Reasoning Models Read Some and Or Literally

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: When a speaker says ``some students passed'', listeners infer that not all of them did. Reasoning models now let users decide how long a model thinks before it answers, but we do not know what extra thinking does to such everyday inferences. We study this directly: we keep a model's weights fixed, change only how much it thinks, and record which reading it chooses. A second tool cuts the model's own reasoning at successive points and asks for an answer, showing where the reading changes. Thinking makes models read logical words as logic: it cancels the implicatures of \emph{some} (\emph{not all}) and \emph{or} (\emph{not both}) in most tested open reasoning models and in GPT-5, while context-driven inferences such as indirect answers improve. The trace shows why: models first entertain the enriched reading and cancel it later. Answering from that early reading, an exploratory inference-time remedy, recovers these implicatures without losing literal accuracy. Evaluations of reasoning models should measure how they interpret, not only how accurate they are.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: A listener hearing Some boys play usually concludes that not all of them do. Although some remains logically true even if every boy plays, listeners reason that speaker knowing they all play would have said all. This step from what is said to what is meant is pragmatic enrichment, and the inference from some to not all is the textbook case (Grice, 1975). Reasoning models now treat thinking as setting the user controls: mode that can be switched on or off, budget of thinking tokens, or an effort level (Yang et al., 2025; OpenAI et al., 2025; DeepSeek-AI, 2025). More thinking usually helps on mathematics and code. Does it also help model understand what speaker means? Existing evaluations score whether model recovFigure 1: Thinking acts as logic lens on logical words. some and or are read as and , while adequate keeps not good. ers an intended meaning (Hu et al., 2023a; Ruis et al., 2023; Sravanthi et al., 2024). Recent studies report that more thinking can hurt theory of mind (Gong et al., 2026) and that Qwen3 recognizes fewer scalar implicatures in thinking mode (Spinoso-Di Piano et al., 2026). No study yet measures what deliberation does to the reading model chooses when both readings are allowed. Human pragmatics offers two competing predictions. On the effort account, enrichment costs effort, so more thinking should yield more of it (Sperber and Wilson, 1986; Bott and Noveck, 2004). On the default-and-cancel account, an implicature such as some not all arises by default and is cancelled when the context or check of the literal meaning speaks against it (Levinson, 2000). Our idea is simple. Because thinking is setting, we can hold models weights fixed and turn only this dial, as in doseresponse experiment, and record which reading the model chooses (Figure 1). To see where the reading changes, we cut the models own reasoning text, its trace, after its first tokens and ask for an answer at each cut. We apply both tools to 40 open and seven closed reasoning models, on items that separate logical words (some, or, modals) from lexical scales (good/excellent), presuppositions and indirect answers. The headline is that thinking makes models read logical words as logic, while inferences that need the context improve; along the trace, models entertain the enriched reading early and cancel it. Our contributions are as follows: ❶ Thinking Cancels Implicature: Extended reasoning cancels scalar implicatures for some and or across 30/40 open models and GPT-5, as well as in label-free three-way choices (21/24 models). ❷ Diagnostic Protocol: We introduce fixed-weight framework combining doseresponse profiling with traceprefix diagnostic to track interpretation dynamics while controlling for yes-bias. ❸ Entertain, Then Cancel: Models typically entertain pragmatic readings in early reasoning tokens before switching to literal readings in completed outputs. ❹ EarlyTrace Extraction: Extracting answers after the first 128 trace tokens improves accuracy on scalar felicity items across two 8B models without compromising literal performance. ❺ Released Resources: We release new BottNoveck sentences with expert-checked speaker-knowledge scenarios, expanded IMPPRES test sets, full trace logs, and machine-translated German/Chinese slices.

sections.title: 2 Background and Related Work
sections.content: Two kinds of implicature. Grice (1975) separated generalized implicatures, which word carries unless the context blocks them (some not all, or not both), from particularized ones, which arise only in specific context (I wore gloves in reply to Did you leave fingerprints? means no). Generalized implicatures attach both to logical words and to lexical scales such as good/excellent, whose enrichment rates vary widely across scales (van Tiel et al., 2016). Three predictions for thinking model. The effort account treats every implicature as an inference that costs processing effort (Sperber and Wilson, 1986). Adults who reject Some elephants are mammals respond more slowly, and they reject it less often under time pressure or memory load (Bott and Noveck, 2004; De Neys and Schaeken, 2007; Marty and Chemla, 2013), although this is contested (Grodner et al., 2010; Degen and Tanenhaus, 2015). If thinking tokens act as processing Figure 2: Thinking makes some more literal in most open reasoning models. Vermilion: counted literal shift; blue: more pragmatic (Figure 11). resources, more thinking should mean more enrichment. The default-and-cancel account holds generalized implicatures as defaults that listener cancels when the context or check of the truth conditions speaks against them (Levinson, 2000). If model spends its thinking on checking strict entailment, it should cancel the implicatures of logical words, while particularized implicatures, reachable only by inference, should hold or improve. third, developmental view notes that children accept underinformative some more frequently than adults (Noveck, 2001). If enrichment tracks competence, thinking may amplify models existing preference, with direction that changes with capability. We use default for the reading chosen without thinking and cancel for shift towards the literal reading as thinking grows, without committing to cognitive mechanism. Section D.1 lists the pre-registered hypotheses and falsifiers. Prior evidence in language models. Chain-ofthought prompts improve implicature resolution (Kim et al., 2023; Ruis et al., 2023), yet chain-ofthought was also seen to encourage literal interpretations (Park et al., 2024). More reasoning lowers theory-of-mind accuracy (Gong et al., 2026), and in ImplicatureX Qwen3s thinking mode recognises fewer scalar implicatures and more cancellations at one budget (Spinoso-Di Piano et al., 2026). These studies measure accuracy at fixed settings. We measure the reading chosen as doseresponse on fixed weights, separate implicature types, and locate the change in the trace and in training (Section E.1).

sections.title: Literal
sections.content: This section shows that thinking makes logical words literal, that the shift survives every analysis choice, where in the trace it happens, and at which training stage the literal default appears.

sections.title: Some and Or
sections.content: Thinking reduces the pragmatic reading of some, or, or both in most models, whereas other inference types behave differently. Table 1 reports the major open families (see also Figure 9), while Figure 2 and Figure 8 detail the item families. Each effect compares natural thinking with thinking off, or with forced-empty thinking block for models without switch; for gpt-oss and closed models it compares the highest with the lowest dose. Natural thinking changes the pragmatic reading of some in Qwen3-8B by 28.2 pp (95% CI 41.0 to 16.7) and that of or by 36.4 pp; in Qwen3-32B the changes are 51.3 and 46.5 pp. High reasoning effort does the same in gpt-oss-20b (30.8 and 24.7 pp against low effort), and in OLMo-3-32B-Think the some reading changes by 11.5 pp. It holds in DeepSeeks distilled thinkers too, which always think: against forced-empty thinking block, natural thinking changes the some reading of R1-Distill-Llama-8B by 50.0 pp and of R1-Distill-Llama-70B by 50.0 pp, and the newest distilled model, DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B, by 24.4 pp. Across 40 open reasoning models, the shift on some or or is significant (95% CI excluding 0, uncorrected) and survives the pre-declared format and polarity checks in 30; 4 models move the other way, 1 shifts only in the Yes/No format, and 5 show no significant change  (Table 12)  . The count applies counting rule declared before the full-roster runs; the outcome of the preregistered aggregate test is reported separately in Section D.2. Models outside the count are discussed in Section C.1. On the held-out half of the full IMPPRES sets (300 items per word), the changes for Qwen3-8B are 37.7 pp for some and 37.7 pp for or, which replicates the core result. sections.title: 4.2 Sensitivity Analysis: The Shift Survives
sections.content: Stopping, Baseline, Format and Item Choices Full-length thinking lowers the pragmatic reading of some and or under every analysis choice  (Table 2)  : with forced-empty block as the baseline, under either stopping procedure, on the held-out full sets and in three-way choice without Yes/No labels, in both Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B. Along the budget (Figure 5) the reading of some first rises, by 37.2 pp at 128 tokens, and falls below its nothinking level only beyond 512 tokens (21.8 pp at 1024): mirroring the trace result (Section 4.3). Four further checks, on how thinking stops, the baseline, answer bias and speaker knowledge, are in Section C.1. The shift persists under both stopping procedures and in three-way choice without Yes/No labels. The three-way prompt asks whether the implicature follows from the sentence, so it removes answer polarity but also moves the question from speaker belief to inference; we use it as polarity check rather than framing-matched replication (prompts in Section B.4).

Table 3 reports the scores across every stage of three lineages without deliberation (using answer log-probabilities), where we measure the within-stage thinking effect wherever applicable. Post-training for reasoning moves the default reading of some, at stage and in direction that depend on the recipe. In OLMo-3, the pragmatic default falls from 75.6% in the base model to 39.7% after supervised fine-tuning on thinking traces, whereas reinforcement learning on math from the same base (RLZero) leaves it at 78.2%. In Tülu-3 the change comes with preference tuning (DPO), from 46.2% to 14.1%, and the following reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) leaves it there. sections.title: 5 Selective Thinking for Scalar Items
sections.content: (Exploratory) If thinking first entertains an implicature and then cancels it, the reading to keep is already in the trace. For questions that ask what speaker of some or or sentence believes, we take the answer the model gives after the first 128 tokens of its own trace instead of the answer after the completed trace; every other item keeps the natural-thinking answer. Routing reads only the prompt (the question template and the speakers sentence), never the dataset or label. On routed items the answer comes entirely from the prefix (weight = 1 on the prefix distribution), and the score is the mean of speakermeaning and literal-gold accuracy, each averaged equally over its sets. The remedy is exploratory, not pre-registered: its weight was selected on development items after two earlier exploratory rounds, frozen, and evaluated once on held-out template families of Qwen3-8B and DeepSeek-R1-0528-

sections.title: 6 Discussion
sections.content: What thinking does to meaning. The results fit the default-and-cancel account better than uniformly rising enrichment. If thinking only supplied resources for implicatures, scalar enrichment would rise; instead it falls on some and or, rises on lexical scales in larger Qwen3 models, is mixed elsewhere, and presuppositions and indirect answers improve. The traces show the predicted order: the enriched reading appears early, in smaller models even strengthened, before the final answer rejects it. Models spend thinking on strict entailment for some and or and override what the speaker meant. This matches earlier observations: the drop in scalar-implicature recognition with more cancellations in ImplicatureX (Spinoso-Di Piano et al., 2026), the literal drift under prompted chain-ofthought (Park et al., 2024), and the gains from Gricean prompts on context-driven implicatures (Kim et al., 2023; Sato et al., 2025). Why it matters. The implicatures thinking reduces are textbook cases of everyday enrichment: some for not all, or for not both. With thinking on, an assistant more often treats some of the tests failed as allowing that all failed, yet answers indirect questions more accurately. Because both readings are licensed, single-answer accuracy benchmarks cannot separate change of interpretation from loss of competence. Evaluations should report the reading chosen alongside accuracy, and training should keep the reading speaker intends where the context warrants it. Who differs. Not every model follows the pattern in every format: Granite-3.3 and Llama-3.1Nemotron-Nano-8B read some more pragmatically in the Yes/No format, and the smallest Qwen3 models and Phi-4-mini-reasoning lose lexical scales as well. With the stage results, this shows that longer deliberation need not produce the literal shift.

sections.title: 7 Conclusion
sections.content: In this work, we investigated whether giving reasoning model more time to think makes it more pragmatic, as the effort account of human enrichment posits, or more literal. On fixed weights, thinking reduces the implicatures of some and or in most open models and in GPT-5, while presuppositions and indirect answers improve and larger Qwen3 models read lexical scales more pragmatically. Early trace prefixes give the enriched reading and completed traces the literal one, and checkpoint comparisons locate the drop in specific posttraining stages. The diagnostic also points to remedy: answering from the reading the model entertains early, rather than the one it settles on, recovers scalar implicatures on held-out items without touching literal accuracy. Reasoning models can now be studied as listeners whose deliberation we control; the dose protocol and the trace diagnostic measure changes in interpretation that accuracy alone cannot distinguish, and locate them inside the reasoning trace.

sections.title: Limitations
sections.content: Scope and causality. The graded doseresponse major rests on Qwen3 and gpt-oss, the open models with thinking switch or effort levels; the other open models are compared against forced-empty thinking block they were not trained on, and closed models only through their APIs. The training-stage results compare checkpoints and are correlational, and the trace probe intervenes on traces rather than reading an internal state, so neither identifies mechanism. All headline items are in English; machine-translated German and Chinese slice (Section C.1) shows the same drop. Measurement. We measure the reading model endorses under forced-choice framings, and the format matters: the direction for Claude models reverses between formats. Free-form answers could not be coded reliably by LLM raters (best agreement of an LLM rater with the human consensus labels κ = 0.57), so every headline result uses forced choices. The exploratory remedy of Section 5 is tested on two 8B models that share base model, so its generality across lineages and scales is untested. The human labels are consensus labels on sample; there is no independent double annotation, so inter-annotator agreement is not reported.

sections.title: Ethical considerations
sections.content: Artefacts. We use publicly released models and datasets under their licences (Section A.2). IMPPRES is licensed for non-commercial use, and two stimulus repositories carry no licence file; we use them for research only, cite their authors, and redistribute only item identifiers and our own new items. We release, under open licences at https://github.com/kouzhizhuo/ entertain-then-cancel, the new category sentences and the 50 speaker-knowledge scenarios; the polarity-flipped and three-way variants of the IMPPRES some/or items, as identifiers plus our templates; the code, prompts and all model traces; and the machine-translated German and Chinese slice, flagged as not human-verified. NOPE, which states no licence, is not redistributed by us. Human participants. No participants were recruited. The only human labels are consensus labels from panel of five or more annotators with PhD-level training in related fields, agreed through discussion; an author recorded them with software tool. They cover blind audit of subset of model answers, the speaker-knowledge scenarios and 20 Chinese translations. No personal data were collected or used. Implications. The finding concerns how assistants interpret users. If thinking modes make models read underinformative or indirect utterances literally, users may receive answers that are technically correct but miss what they meant. Deployers who switch thinking on by default for conversational use should evaluate interpretation, not only accuracy. We see no dual-use risk beyond this. AI assistance. AI assistants were used for code writing and polish but the whole research is design and checked by researchers.

sections.title: B Experimental Setup
sections.content: How items are built and read out, how every run is decoded and audited, the prior-work baselines and the verbatim prompts. B.1 Method Details This section gives the item sets, readouts, data splits and statistical tests in full. Models and checkpoints. The primary manipulation needs model whose thinking can be switched and dosed without changing its weights. Qwen3 has hybrid thinking mode in which the no-thinking template differs from the thinking template only by an empty thinking block (Yang et al., 2025). We therefore use Qwen3-4B, 8B and 14B as the primary models, and 1.7B and 32B for size. The Qwen3 size ladder is also training-recipe ladder: the 0.6B14B models are built by strongto-weak distillation from larger models, whereas the 32B and 235B models go through the full four-stage pipeline with reasoning and general RL (Yang et al., 2025, 4.5). Size and recipe are therefore confounded within Qwen3, and we separate them with two same-recipe size pairs, OLMo-37B-Think vs. OLMo-3-32B-Think and gpt-oss-20b vs. 120b. As capability covariate we use each models accuracy on fixed subset of MATH-500 without thinking. gpt-oss-20b and 120b add second family with three reasoning-effort levels (OpenAI et al., 2025). We use them only if the realised reasoning length grows monotonically with the level on held-out items. To locate the training origin, we score checkpoints along base SFT DPO RLVR lineages: OLMo-2 (Team OLMo et al., 2024), OLMo-3-Think (Team Olmo et al., 2025) and Tülu-3 from SFT onward (Lambert et al., 2024). We also score the OLMo-3 RL-Zero series, which applies RLVR to one base model in five reward domains (math, code, instruction following, general, mixed), at six log-spaced steps each. Distilled thinkers (DeepSeek-AI, 2025) and zero-RL pairs (Zeng et al., 2025; Hu et al., 2025) are secondary contrast, because their weights differ from their bases in more than training stage (Yu et al., 2026). All models are open weights and ungated. Section A.1 lists identifiers and revisions. Items fall into three classes. GeneralData. ized implicatures (GCIs) comprise BottNoveckstyle category sentences written for this study (six sentence types per category triple, every item screened by two Claude-family LLM raters and an open-weight co-rater (Qwen332B) on the same items, with disagreements dropped the Qwen3-32B co-rater pass is in exp/gold/item_screen_qwen32b.jsonl; Section B.2); scalar-diversity sentences with human inference rates per scale (van Tiel et al., 2016; Gotzner et al., 2018; Pankratz and van Tiel, 2021; Hu et al., 2023b); and IMPPRES implicature pairs whose logical and pragmatic labels differ, plus fresh paraphrased minimal pairs (Jeretic et al., 2020). Particularized implicatures (PCIs) come from PragMega (Hu et al., 2023a), LUDWIG (Ruis et al., 2023), Fig-QA (Liu et al., 2022) and six PUB tasks (Sravanthi et al., 2024). Presupposition items come from IMPPRES. We also run all of ImplicatureX as replication set (Spinoso-Di Piano et al., 2026). Released sets that predate the thinking models may be contaminated. We therefore report headline GCI numbers on the fresh items and treat released sets as replications; the within-item contrast between thinking conditions does not depend on whether an item was seen in training. Items are split 50/50 into development and test halves, stratified by set. Every finding is reported on the test half. Sources, licences and item counts are listed in Section B.2. Framings. Scalar items are asked two ways. Felicity framings make the literal answer pragmatic failure and are primary. For IMPPRES this is an inference question (Would you conclude that the speaker believes . . . ?). For the category sentences it is ternary judgement (completely right / bit wrong / completely wrong) and 17 rating, with binary felicity (Is this good way to describe the facts?) as comparison. The truth framing (Is the sentence true or false?) is the logic-mode comparison (Section D.1). PCI items use their native meaning format (What did the speaker mean?). For H2c, subset of PCI items is also asked in ImplicatureXs form, Is this interpretation true or false?. Multiple-choice options are shuffled on every trial. subset is also answered without options, to rule out option matching (Gong et al., 2026). Because LLM coding of these open answers did not reach the pre-declared agreement with human audit, we report them descriptively (Section B.2). Reference labels for these answers are reference labels by two LLM raters from different model families, adjudicated: Claude-family model and Qwen3-32B, with disagreements resolved by second Claude-family model. We report their inter-rater κ, and the judges agreement with them as consistency. Family overlaps are disclosed: Qwen3-32B belongs to the family of the Qwen3 models whose answers it labels; the judge for gpt-oss answers is Qwen3-32B itself, so that agreement is partly self-agreement; the judge for Qwen3 answers, gpt-oss-120b, overlaps with neither rater. The only human labels are consensus labels from blind expert audit of 50 of these answers and 24 speaker-knowledge scenarios, which carries the validity claim (Section B.2). Thinking manipulations. No thinking (NT) uses the models own switch, which leaves the chat template byte-identical apart from the empty thinking block. Two other ways of disabling thinking serve as checks. Capped budgets stop the thinking block at {64, . . . , 2048} tokens and append Qwen3s own stop phrase (Yang et al., 2025). Because that phrase mentions limited time, plain cap that appends only the closing tag controls for the time-pressure cue. Natural thinking (NAT) is uncapped. Capping truncates thoughts, so we also stratify eight natural samples per item by their realised length, and we plot every effect against realised rather than nominal length. Budget forcing beyond the natural stopping point (Muennighoff et al., 2025) tests whether more thinking than the model chooses continues the trend. Capped and length-stratified budgets change only the number of thinking tokens, on fixed weights and fixed template; the thinking switch and gpt-oss effort levels also change the template or system prompt, so we treat them as mode contrasts and rest dose response claims on the budget contrasts. Sampling settings are identical across conditions (T =0.6, top-p 0.95, top-k 20), so thinking is not confounded with temperature. Generation uses vLLM (Kwon et al., 2023). Intent-Seeded and controls. Interventions Thinking (IST) places one fixed sentence about speaker intent at the start of the thinking block, or just before it closes. Its controls are neutral sentence about careful, step-by-step reasoning and logic sentence about checking what the words strictly entail, both token-matched to the intent seed (26 Qwen3 tokens); first run used shorter neutral seed (16 tokens), reported separately and not treated as length-matched. We compare IST with prompted deliberation on the same weights zero-shot chain-of-thought with thinking off: (Kojima et al., 2022), Gricean instructions and Grice-maxim chain-of-thought (Sato et al., 2025; Kim et al., 2023), few-shot prompting (Ruis et al., 2023), an adapted RSA-style chain-of-thought (Tsvilodub et al., 2025), and self-consistency at matched token cost (Wang et al., 2023). For H2b, the critical sentences are preceded by contexts in which the speaker has full or partial knowledge (Goodman and Stuhlmüller, 2013). For H4, the load is unrelated background text (512 or 2,048 words from one of two genres) placed before the item, followed by an instruction to ignore it. Each critical item has comprehension check (an entailment paraphrase) and meta-pragmatic probe (Would speaker who says this normally mean . . . ?), so literal answer can be separated from failure to understand. Section B.2 gives every prompt verbatim. Closed-model API calls cost about $105 in total. Statistics. Each condition is run with three decoding seeds. Tables report the mean standard deviation over seeds of the item-averaged rate. Intervals in the text and figures are 95% cluster-bootstrap confidence intervals over items (10,000 resamples, paired across conditions). The pre-registered primary tests were mixed-effects logistic regressions with by-item random effects; as implemented (Section D.3), they are logistic regressions with itemclustered standard errors, one per model, with the log thinking budget, the phenomenon class and their interaction as predictors. Equivalence is tested with two one-sided tests at 3 pp, trends over training steps with Spearmans ρ and permutation pvalues, and alignment with human rates with Spearmans ρ. p-values are Holm-corrected within each pre-registered family of models. Secondary analyses are uncorrected and labelled as such. Every finding is computed on held-out half of the items; the other half was used only to fix prompts and parsing. Hypotheses, thresholds and exclusion rules were fixed before the main runs (Section D.3). B.2 Experimental Details This section documents decoding, answer parsing, judging and the human audit. Items, sources and licences. The BottNoveckstyle category sentences (category triples, each in six sentence types) and the 50 speaker-knowledge scenarios were written for this study. Every new item was screened by two Claude-family LLM raters against written criteria (the universal statement is true without common exceptions; the partial control is true and clearly partial; the false control is false under every sense, including cladistic taxonomy; no lexical ambiguity). An item was kept only if both raters accepted it or accepted the same fix. Twenty speaker-knowledge scenarios are also part of the human audit below. Compute. Generation and judging ran on NVIDIA H800 GPUs ( 200 GPU-hours in total); the GRPO runs used 4-GPU jobs with verl 0.9.1. Prompts. Every prompt template is released with the code. Decoding and compute. =0.6, top-p 0.95, topk 20 in every condition; three seeds; maximum of 8,192 thinking tokens for natural thinking. Reference labels and the human audit. Open answers are coded as pragmatic, literal, or hedged/other. Reference labels: two LLM raters from different model families (a Claude-family model and Qwen3-32B) labelled pool of 294 answers blind to condition. Disagreements were adjudicated by second Claude-family model with logged reason. Inter-rater agreement: κ = 0.18. Judges: The judge we ran, gpt-oss-20b, agrees with the human consensus labels at κ = 0.33 [0.12, 0.54], below the pre-declared acceptance rule ( 0.70), so open-answer results are reported descriptively and every headline result uses forced-choice formats. Human audit: panel of five or more annotators with PhD-level training in related fields agreed, through discussion, one consensus label for each of 50 answers from the same pool and 24 speaker-knowledge scenarios (12 with full and 12 with partial access). The sample was stratified and random with fixed seed (answers stratified by reference class, oversampling the rarer classes), and the annotators were blind to model, condition and all model labels. An author recorded the consensus labels with software tool. The labels are not independent annotations, so no inter-annotator agreement is reported. These are the only human labels in the paper. Scenarios: judgements the consensus matched the intended reading in every scenario (100.0%, Wilson 95% lower bound 86.2%): some was judged misleading whenever the speaker had checked every object and fine whenever the speaker had not. This meets the pre-declared validity bar (80%, lower bound 70%). Open-answer coding: agreement of each LLM rater with the human consensus labels, post-stratified to the pool, is κ = 0.57 [0.34, 0.79] for the Claude-family rater (accuracy 77.4%) and κ = 0.14 [0.02, 0.31] for Qwen332B (0.03 with option orders averaged). All doses of model use the same answer extraction. GPT-5 becomes more literal with effort in both answer formats, and the shift cannot come from bias towards Yes: without the utterance its Yes rate rises with effort, which would raise, not lower, the pragmatic rate in the Yes/No format. For the Claude models the picture depends on the format. Under the Yes/No inference framing their pragmatic rate rises with thinking, but in three-way forced choice it falls (Sonnet) or stays flat (Opus). For Claude Sonnet 4.6, much of the Yes/No rise is shift towards answering Yes: the Yes rate also rises without the utterance, and the pragmatic rate falls when the question is flipped. Claude Opus 4.8 shows small shift towards the pragmatic answer under both polarities. The same two checks explain the two open models whose pragmatic rate rises with thinking. For Magistral-Small, the Yes rate without the utterance rises by 14.1 pp [10.1, 18.3], and with the flipped question its pragmatic rate falls by 52.9 pp [59.0, 46.7], so its rise is shift towards Yes. Of those that move the other way, Magistral-Small mostly shifts towards answering Yes: with the question flipped so that No is pragmatic, its pragmatic rate falls by 52.9 pp. Granite-3.3 and Llama-3.1-NemotronNano-8B move towards the pragmatic reading only in the Yes/No format: in three-way choice both turn literal (some: 22.8 and 8.7 pp; Table 9). The rise of openPangu-Embedded-7B-model is, like Magistrals, shift towards answering Yes: with the question flipped its pragmatic rate falls, and in the three-way choice it is flat. In the threeway format, which has no Yes/No labels, 21 of the 24 models with full-set run shift towards the literal reading on some or or, and only two rise on one word: SmolLM3-3B from its floor (some: +3.9 pp) and Qwen3.5-0.8B on some (+10.7 pp), whose or reading falls (8.3 pp). openPangu-Embedded7B-V1.1, null on the core items, shifts on its full held-out set (some: 15.4 pp) and in the three-way choice (8.4 pp). Four robustness checks. How thinking stops. Qwen3s stop phrase mentions limited time. Stopping the trace with only the closing tag gives the same shift at 1,024 tokens (24.4 against 21.8 pp with the stop phrase). The baseline. Against forced-empty thinking block instead of the models switch, natural thinking changes the some reading of Qwen3-8B by 39.7 pp. Answer bias. shift towards answering No could imitate literal reading. For GPT-5 the opposite holds: without the speakers sentence, its rate of answering Yes rises with effort, which would push the pragmatic rate up, not down  (Table 7)  . For Qwen3-8B answer polarity does matter: with the question reworded so that No is the pragmatic answer, thinking raises the pragmatic rate by 22.7 pp from floor near zero. In three-way forced choice, which has no Yes/No labels, thinking still lowers the pragmatic reading at every Qwen3 size, in Qwen3-8B by 34.0 pp for some and 13.8 pp for or (Section B.3). Speaker knowledge. pragmatic listener enriches more when the speaker has checked every case (Goodman and Stuhlmüller, 2013); the scenarios we built for this were screened blind to condition by the annotator panel, whose consensus judged some misleading in every full-knowledge scenario and fine in every partial-knowledge one (24 scenarios). Most models make little use of this knowledge: with thinking, the gap between full and partial knowledge is 4.2 pp in Qwen3-32B. The one model that uses it without much deliberation, gpt-oss-120b (84.0 pp at low effort), uses it less at high effort (62.5 pp). This section gives the full per-model results and additional analyses behind the main text. Trace probe beyond Qwen3. Figure 7 shows the trace probe on the newest generation. In Figure 4d, the jump of Phi-4-reasonings lexical-scale reading after 32 tokens (40.6%) appears only in the sampled answers; the answer-position log-odds does not move (1.08 with an empty trace, 1.00 after 32 tokens). The same early jump of the lexical-scale line appears in both Qwen3.5 models, over the first 3264 tokens and with tight intervals (41.7% and 43.6% in Qwen3.5-4B, 44.1% in Qwen3.59B), so it is systematic early-prefix effect, not noise. It is confined to the sampled answers: the answer-position log-odds stays negative, that is literal-favouring, and moves little (Qwen3.5-9B: 2.13 with an empty trace, 1.17 after 32 tokens). The line returns to the no-thinking level by the end. For the further families (Figure 6), SkyworkOR1 is the exception: its pragmatic reading drops within the first 32 tokens (or: 75.8% to 45.5%) and then stays flat, so there is no early phase of endorsement. Intent-Seeded Thinking (IST) opens the thinking block with one fixed sentence about what the speaker intends to convey; two control sentences of the same length (26 tokens) ask for careful step-by-step reasoning or for checking what the words strictly entail (Section B.1). We call them GCIs and PCIs. The two major post-Gricean theories disagree about GCIs. On the default view (Levinson, 2000), GCI is generated automatically and cancelled only when the context contradicts it. On the relevance-theoretic view (Sperber and Wilson, 1986), every implicature is an inference drawn when it pays off in relevance, and drawing it costs processing effort. Both treat PCIs as context-driven inferences. Adults pay for enrichment; children often do not make it. Adults who reject an underinformative sentence such as Some elephants are mammals take longer than adults who accept it, and short response deadline yields fewer rejections (Bott and Noveck, 2004). concurrent memory readings on every phenomenon we test. On the default-and-cancel account, the model holds GCIs as defaults and spends deliberation on truth-conditional verification, habit that training with verifiable rewards (RLVR) plausibly rewards. Thinking then cancels GCIs while it improves PCIs, whose pragmatic reading can only be reached by inference. On the capability account, deliberation amplifies whichever competence dominates the trace, so the sign of the effect on GCIs depends on the models capability, much as enrichment depends on age in children. The theory question is therefore: Do reasoning models pay the cost of enrichment, or the cost of cancelling it, and does that depend on capability? Test-time thinking is dose of deliberation on fixed weights. If pragmatic enrichment in language models is effortful, more thinking yields more enrichment on every phenomenon; if training with verifiable rewards installs default-and-cancel profile, thinking cancels generalized implicatures while it improves particularized ones; if deliberation amplifies existing competence, the sign on generalized implicatures reverses with capability. sections.title: E Related Work
sections.content: The extended discussion of related work. E.1 Related Work This section reviews related work on implicature, reasoning models and test-time compute. Test-time reasoning and social understanding. Several studies find that reasoning does not transfer to social cognition. Reasoning variants of Qwen3 and DeepSeek do no better than their non-reasoning counterparts on theory-of-mind benchmarks, and o3s accuracy on higher-order belief questions falls as reasoning effort rises (Gong et al., 2026). Reasoning models also trail older models on theoryof-mind variants of cognitive-science experiments (Lupu et al., 2025), and the gains they do show are better described as robustness to prompt variation than as new ability (de Haan et al., 2026b,a). For presupposition, models with stronger reasoning give less human-like projection judgements (Azin et al., 2026), and reasoning adds only 2 11 points on queries with false presuppositions (Sathyanathan et al., 2026). On implicature the record is mixed. The closest observation is incidental: in ImplicatureX, benchmark of implicature recognition and cancellation, Qwen3 in thinking mode at 512-token budget recognises fewer scalar implicatures than the same weights without thinking, and recognises cancellations more often (Spinoso-Di Piano et al., 2026). Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompts built on Grices maxims, on relevance theory or on the Rational Speech Act model improve implicature resolution and number-word interpretation (Kim et al., 2023; Sato et al., 2025; Tsvilodub et al., 2025); CoT lifts GPT-4 to human average on binary implicatures (Ruis et al., 2023); and training on counterfactual reasoning traces helps further (Park et al., 2026; Sravanthi et al., 2025). Yet CoT was also observed to encourage literal interpretations in Korean (Park et al., 2024). Unlike ImplicatureX, which observes the drop at single budget on 46 items without intervals and does not treat it as thinking effect, and unlike Gong et al. (2026), who study the same manipulations on theory-of-mind accuracy, we treat the thinking budget as controlled dose, measure the reading chosen under felicity and truth framings, show that the effect dissociates by implicature type, trace it to an entertain-then-cancel trajectory inside the trace and to specific post-training stages (thinking SFT in OLMo-3, preference tuning in Tülu-3), and test four pre-registered remedies under matched controls. Pragmatics in language models. Benchmarks cover implicature, indirect speech, irony, metaphor, humour, deceit and presupposition (Hu et al., 2023a; Ruis et al., 2023; Sravanthi et al., 2024; Jeretic et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2022); see Ma et al. (2025) for survey. When models err on these items, their errors favour the literal reading over distractors (Hu et al., 2023a). Work on scalar implicature links model expectations over alternatives to human inference rates (Schuster et al., 2020; Hu et al., 2023b), probes scalar diversity (Lin et al., 2024), and steers graded interpretations through activations (Cho, 2026). Thinking and instruct models have also been compared on quantifier production, across models (Montero et al., 2025). Pragmatic competence rises from base to SFT and preference-tuned checkpoints (Yu et al., 2026). This is why comparisons across training stages confound deliberation with post-training. Unlike these works, we treat the inference budget as the independent variable, hold the weights fixed for the primary contrast, and extend the stage analysis from supervised fine-tuning through preference tuning to RLVR. Overthinking and side effects of reasoning training. Longer reasoning can lower accuracy on easy problems, on tasks with distractors and on deduction (Chen et al., 2024; Gema et al., 2025; Ghosal et al., 2025; Lee et al., 2026; Sui et al., 2025). Explicit reasoning also degrades instruction following (Li et al., 2025), and CoT hurts where deliberation hurts humans (Liu et al., 2024), while its benefits concentrate on math and symbolic tasks (Sprague et al., 2025). Reinforcement fine-tuning has side effects of its own: it lowers refusals on unanswerable questions (Song et al., 2025), can raise hallucination (Yao et al., 2025), and may sharpen what the base model already does rather than extend it (Yue et al., 2025). Budget forcing (Muennighoff et al., 2025), hybrid thinking modes (Yang et al., 2025) and effort levels (OpenAI et al., 2025) make the amount of reasoning controllable; recent work also asks how reasoning changes social behaviours such as sycophancy (Feng et al., 2026). These works define harm as lower accuracy on tasks with one correct answer. Our outcome is choice between two readings that are both licensed by the sentence. The direction of the shift, not its size, is what distinguishes the two theories. The processing cost of enrichment in humans. Human evidence that scalar enrichment is effortful comes from response times, deadlines and dualtask load (Bott and Noveck, 2004; De Neys and Schaeken, 2007; Dieussaert et al., 2011; Marty and Chemla, 2013; Tomlinson et al., 2013), and from development (Noveck, 2001). Counter-evidence shows that the cost depends on context and on the availability of alternatives (Breheny et al., 2006; Grodner et al., 2010; Degen and Tanenhaus, 2015). Enrichment rates also vary widely across scales (van Tiel et al., 2016; Gotzner et al., 2018; Pankratz and van Tiel, 2021), and probabilistic models treat enrichment as inference about cooperative speaker (Frank and Goodman, 2012; Goodman and Frank, 2016; Goodman and Stuhlmüller, 2013).
